answer: Moshi’s architecture consists of three core parts: a bespoke text‑language‑model backbone named Helium; a neural audio codec called Mimi that uses residual vector quantization and distills semantic knowledge from a self‑supervised speech model; and a streaming, hierarchical generator that produces semantic and acoustic tokens for both the user and Moshi, together with time‑aligned text tokens for Moshi when using Inner Monologue [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6].
